work.objective: Independently fix Bun/OpenTUI Backspace through the reliable global key path by invoking native TextareaRenderable editing operations, while preserving printable text, Tab and Enter behavior; leave real PTY proof to the verifier.
constraints: Use repository-relative paths for every read, search, edit and command.
Only modify the three allowlisted input-prompt files; do not modify Ink, dependencies, lockfiles, Marshal state, commit, push, publish, use network access or start subagents.

Do not read, search, list, compare, import or copy any R1/R2/R3 worktree, patch, transcript, WorkerResult, ReviewPacket or Marshal run artifact; implement independently from the frozen base branch requirements.

Never implement deletion by slicing or reconstructing JavaScript strings. For Backspace use TextareaRenderable.deleteCharBackward(); for word deletion use the native deleteWordBackward operation when the decoded modifier semantics require it.

Because native focused capture is unreliable in this renderer, Backspace must be handled in the global useKeyboard path, followed by preventDefault to avoid duplicate handling. Other editing/navigation keys and Tab must not be inserted as printable bytes.
The printable fallback must reject ctrl, meta, option, super and hyper modifiers, all C0/C1/DEL bytes, escape sequences and named editing/navigation keys while preserving ASCII, CJK and emoji input.
Worker checks are limited to unit/OpenTUI vitest, CLI typecheck/build and git diff --check; do not launch Bun, expect, PTY diagnostics or background processes.
If an operation is denied, do not retry that path; use an allowed equivalent or report blocked.
context: The user reproduced Backspace not deleting in the Bun/OpenTUI composer.

Two independent native traces rendered ZXQ but produced no frame after DEL+Enter, including after defaultTextareaKeyBindings were composed. The component already documents that focused native capture can fail, while the global handler reliably receives printable keys and Enter.
The clean solution is to invoke the textarea's native editing API from that reliable global path, not manually mutate its text.
The verifier waits for ready, types ZXQ, sends DEL then Enter, requires submitted ZX, and exits with Ctrl+C.
